title: Rust ground mist is the look's fog, never a translucent plane above the floor
note: Mist and shafts are [render.look] fog (density, height falloff); a translucent plane at knee height reads as a flood line.
intent: A translucent horizontal quad half a metre up cuts every crate and character at one height, which the eye reads as water. In genex the air is the look's fog: fog_density and the height falloff in genex.toml [render.look], or RenderConfig::from_build().fog(Fog::default().with_density(..).with_height(..)) in code. Shape a floor-hugging mist with the height falloff rather than more density, keep interiors thin (0.004-0.01: 0.02 washes a room blue), and let high and ultra light it as a volume with sun shafts through windows. Never stack transparent planes, cubes or cards for haze; if a judge names a haze or water line, look for one in the level code first.

check.ask: Is there a flat translucent layer cutting through objects at one height, like a water line or a sheet of haze?
check.note: No haze plane: ground fog is the look's fog with a height falloff, never a translucent plane above the floor.

port: Only the facet that owns the look sets fog; no other facet draws a translucent horizontal plane above the floor.

evidence.note: The air is the look's fog; high and ultra light it as a volume; never fake haze with stacked transparent planes.
The three.js recipe arena.no-haze-planes, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
